newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Bund volatilities suffer after data.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Bund volatilities suffer after data.

text.p: Implied volatility levels on options on Bunds slid lower on Thursday after release of German M3 data and a Bundesbank council meeting, brokers said.
"Volatility is getting absolutely smacked," said Steven West, broker at GNI in London. "It has come off quiet sharply and we've seen aggressive paper sellers, local sellers as well."
Brokers quoted at-the-money implied volatility for October, which expires on Monday, at 3.9 to 4.1 percent compared with 5.1 percent early in the session.
Synthetically October vols had sold as cheaply as 3.64 percent on puts during the session, West said.

Further out, volatility in November was at 4.46 to 4.62 percent for November, off from 4.8 percent earlier, while for December vols loss was not so aggressive at 4.7 to 4.8 percent compared with 4.8 to 4.93 percent earlier.
A French broker in London agreed everything had been well bid early in the session prior to the release of M3 and the Bundesbank news.

German M3 grew an annualised 8.7 percent in August, compared with forecast growth of 8.0 percent and growth of 8.6 percent in July. The German Ifo survey also showed some growth in the business climate in both East and West Germany.

The Bundesbank, which did not call a news conference after its meeting, left the repo rate unchanged at 3.0 percent for the next three weeks and held the discount and lombard rates at 2.50 percent and 4.50 percent respectively.
"When these (events) came out the market settled around 98.00 and volatility started to come off and that's the situation we find ourselves in at the moment," the broker said.
Since the figures, he said the market had been quiet.
"These things have a way of finding an equilibrium. It's come off and there is very little going on at the moment," said the French broker.
Immediately after the data, brokers said a Japanese bank had been sellers of the December 98.00 straddle.
By 1221 GMT, around 1,000 lots of October 98.00 calls and almost 3,000 lots of October 98.00 puts had been traded according to LIFFE data on Reuters.
Before and up to the figures, selling of November 97.00 puts had been a feature of the session, brokers said.
December Bund futures were at 98.07 by 1224 GMT, down four basis points on the day.
